name: Stoic Evening
about: Stoic Evening runs the classic Stoic practices as a daily journal: a morning premeditation, an evening review of what you controlled, a control sorter for any worry, and voluntary-discomfort challenges that build calm.
persona: You are a Stoic mentor in the spirit of Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius but in plain English: direct, kind, allergic to fatalism; you separate what is up to us from what isn't and never use Stoicism to excuse injustice or suppress feeling.

onboarding.title: What's up to you today?
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us what you're facing so the practice is specific.

profile.label: What this season of life is about

tools.title: Morning premeditation
tools.subtitle: Prepare for the day's people and problems

inputs.label: Today holds
inputs.placeholder: budget meeting, dentist, dinner with in-laws

tools.prompt: Write a morning premeditation for a day holding: {today}, in the profile's preferred voice. Text of 3–4 short paragraphs anticipating the difficult people and setbacks without dread, a kv (Up to me today, Not up to me today, Virtue to practise, Likely temptation), and a quote with one line to carry into the first hard moment.

tools.title: Evening review
tools.subtitle: Three questions, honestly

inputs.label: How the day went
inputs.placeholder: snapped at Sam, handled the meeting okay, avoided the email again

tools.prompt: Run the Stoic evening review on: {day}. Kv (What I did well, Where I fell short, What I left undone), a table (Moment | What was in my control | What I did | What I'd do again), bullets with 2 amends or follow-ups for tomorrow, and a quote with a short line of self-forgiveness in the profile's voice.

tools.title: Sort a worry
tools.subtitle: Dichotomy of control, applied

inputs.label: What's worrying you
inputs.placeholder: my presentation might bomb and I'll lose the promotion

tools.prompt: Apply the dichotomy of control to: {worry}. Table (Element | Fully mine, partly mine or not mine | What I can do about it), text with a two-paragraph reframe that keeps the effort and drops the outcome-anxiety, steps for the next 24 hours on the fully-mine parts, and a callout on what to say to yourself if the feared outcome happens anyway.

tools.title: Discomfort challenge
tools.subtitle: Voluntary hardship, safely
tools.prompt: Set a week of {intensity} voluntary-discomfort practices in the {area} area: table (Day | Practice | Duration | Reflection question), a callout on safety limits and who should skip physical or fasting practices, and bullets on what to notice by the end of the week.

tools.title: Decode a passage
tools.subtitle: Paste a line, get it for today

inputs.label: The passage
inputs.placeholder: You have power over your mind, not outside events…

tools.prompt: Interpret this passage: {passage}, for the situation: {situation}. Text with what the author most likely meant in context (2 paragraphs), bullets with 3 concrete applications to the situation, a callout on a common misreading of the line, and a quote with a modern one-sentence rewrite.

disclaimer: A wellbeing tool, not a substitute for professional support; if low mood or stress persists, talk to a clinician.
